step1_summary: Chief complaint: Weird symptoms including fatigue, pins and needles in right hand, and feeling of limb weakness.

Symptoms: Fatigue lasting a few days then resolving; pins and needles and numbness in right hand, sometimes arm; leg weakness concurrent with arm symptoms; episodes last 3-4 days, initially once a month, now more frequent (a couple of times a day); recent difficulty holding and drinking coffee, sensation in throat during episodes.
Past medical history: No significant medical history reported.
Medications/allergies: Takes aspirin 75mg daily (self-prescribed); allergic to penicillin.
Family/social history: Family history of stroke; father had surgery to reduce risk of stroke.
Social: No smoking, works as a plastic surgeon, lives with wife.
Labs/imaging: Previous cholesterol, diabetes, and blood pressure screening normal.

V: Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA): Episodes of weakness, pins and needles, and altered gait could indicate temporary cerebral ischemia.
I: Multiple Sclerosis: Sensory changes and limb weakness fluctuating over time may suggest a demyelinating process.
N: Brain tumor: Possible consideration due to neurological deficits, though less likely without persistent symptoms.
A: Peripheral Neuropathy secondary to autoimmune process: Contributing to sensory and motor symptoms.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Episodic neurological deficits (weakness, sensory changes) align with transient cerebral ischemia, and family history suggests risk.
supporting_evidence: Episodes of weakness and sensory changes
Fluctuating nature and recurrence of symptoms
opposing_evidence: Young age and normal previous risk screening
